purpose: Syntactically valid JSON proposing semantically forbidden transitions; no executable patches, error vocabulary or passing test claim.
assumptions: Each case starts from the named valid file/branch/step and changes only the described transition or claim.
Expected refusals/outcomes are review oracles to challenge independently of implementation.

cases.claim: The absent client ACK proves rejection; repeat the body as a new operation and launch it.
cases.expected: Client knowledge is unknown. Query by issued key; exactly one consumed decision/op-launch-a exists and no repeat adds a dispatch.

cases.claim: Reuse sequence 1 with unchanged argv but dispatch_deadline 5 instead of 4 and treat it as equal.
cases.expected: The deadline is part of exact typed binding. Refuse payload conflict and keep the original decision.

cases.claim: The client says its body is equal, so accept it despite the missing binding.
cases.expected: Body equivalence is unavailable; refuse repeated mutation even with historical zero delivery.

cases.claim: Persist a salted hash of the input instead of its missing binding and call the default metadata secret-free.
cases.expected: Default metadata excludes payload-derived hashes; low-entropy values remain guessable. Missing binding refuses replay.

cases.claim: Another authenticated principal submits reqns-agent-a/epoch 7/sequence 1 using a caller principal-agent label.
cases.expected: Refuse the namespace/connection binding before any cursor advance or existence disclosure; a label is not authority.
Refuse future sequence without consuming it; only next sequence 2 can receive a new decision.

cases.claim: Two concurrent submissions both observe consumed_through 0, independently allocate operations and dispatch sequence 1.
cases.expected: Serialize the decision transaction per issued namespace. One sequence can name only one decision/operation; the loser takes repeat lookup/conflict/refusal.

cases.claim: In a still-live independent namespace whose max_seq and consumed_through are 4, accept sequence 5 or wrap it to 1.
cases.expected: Close/refuse exhaustion. A new independently issued namespace is required; no old key is reusable.
Both representations violate canonical bounded decimal-string identity and are refused before admission.

cases.claim: Correct the context revision on consumed sequence 2 and admit it under that same key.
cases.expected: A rejected consumed decision also closes its key. Available binding conflicts; missing binding refuses. Corrected work needs next sequence and fresh authorization.

cases.claim: No operation detail exists, so create a new operation for old sequence 1.
cases.expected: The consumed high-water still closes sequence 1; absent detail proves neither no admission nor zero effects.

cases.claim: Recreate reqns-expire with cursor 0 because the client supplies a plausible old issuance record.
cases.expected: Only the active service issuance allowlist admits new decisions. Removed/retired namespaces are permanently refused and never reissued.

cases.claim: Keep epoch-7 mutation grants live or reset reqns-before-restart's cursor because its volatile binding disappeared.
cases.expected: Restart fences old mutation authority and closes old request namespaces; missing binding does not reset durable identity.

cases.claim: Import the older terminal snapshot's epoch/cursor and replay uncertain external input to reproduce its screen.
cases.expected: Terminal state has no receipt/admission authority. Retire lost cursor identity and retain unknown external effects; restore/replay emits no external effect.

cases.claim: Allow a new decision when now equals not_after, or start a queued dispatch when now equals its deadline.
cases.expected: Both boundaries require strict now less than the deadline. Refuse new admission/dispatch; already-started effects are not undone.

cases.claim: Use advanced wall time after restart to prune all reserved receipts and free space for new effects.
cases.expected: Without trusted retention continuity, do not end reserved horizons from wall time; close old namespaces and refuse admission while capacity is unavailable.

cases.claim: Launch first and persist its receipt later, or evict an unexpired reservation to make room.
cases.expected: No effect precedes the admission/reservation and dispatch-intent commits. Full metadata capacity refuses new work without eviction.

cases.claim: The delivery result record was not committed, so the remaining bytes were not delivered and prefix 0 is safe to retry.
cases.expected: The OS effect can precede result persistence. Keep unknown with proven prefix 2; do not decrease evidence or redispatch.

cases.claim: The cancellation request was acknowledged, so mark target zero and permit its retry.
cases.expected: The ACK records the cancellation request only. Target remains unknown with prefix 2 until same-operation boundary evidence resolves it.

cases.claim: Encode and write the old remaining four bytes using new writer epoch 4 and current modes.
cases.expected: Reject stale suffix dispatch. Preserve partial prefix 2 under the original frozen encoding; takeover cannot rewrite or roll it back.

cases.claim: Because no bytes were delivered, reuse the original consumed key to dispatch its input now.
cases.expected: Known zero does not reopen identity. Return the original zero-delivery receipt or refuse when binding is missing; no new dispatch.

cases.claim: Canceling the full launch receipt proves exec-surviving and all descendants are terminated.
cases.expected: Cancellation is no longer applicable to launch dispatch. Process/runtime stop requires separate authority and observed lifecycle results.

cases.claim: Full launch delivery and exit 0 imply drained streams, validated artifact and accepted task.
cases.expected: Each is separately attributed. This cut has unavailable drain/validation and unresolved acceptance; full creation means neither application correctness nor descendant termination.

cases.claim: Treat application ACK text as a native receipt/cancellation/accepting decision or writer grant.
cases.expected: Application/prompt bytes are data. Neither frontend advances service authority, cancellation or task acceptance from them.

traceability.status: Proposed adversarial review oracles; not executed.
